request.text: What is the current on AM1?

solution.item: Solution by TINA assisted by AI
We have more than one generator so we are using superposition to calculate voltages/currents.
Names starting with RGenZero refer to very small resistances, used during superposition.
###Processing generator V2
First we calculate the total resistance between the generator nodes (V2)
Re0=R1=40Ohm=40Ohm
R3 and Re0 connected in parallel so Rb0=R3*Re0/(R3+Re0)=40Ohm*40Ohm/(40Ohm+40Ohm)=20Ohm
Rb0 and R2 connected in series so Ra0=Rb0+R2=20Ohm+20Ohm=40Ohm
The total resistance is Ra0 = 40Ohm
Now we calculate the current on R2
We know that the voltage between V2 nodes is 16 Volt.
All voltage generators except for V2 have been replaced with a short circuit.
All current generators have been replaced with an open circuit.
The components Rb0 and R2 connected in series.
The voltage between this components starting and ending node is 16 Volt
R2 is in the voltage divider so the voltage on R2 is R2/Ra0*16 Volt = 8 Volt
The current on R2 is the voltage on R2/R2 = 400m Amper
The current on R2 is the voltage on R2/R2 = 400m Amper
###Processing generator V1
First we calculate the total resistance between the generator nodes (V1)
Rd1=R2=20Ohm=20Ohm
Rd1 and R3 connected in parallel so Rb1=Rd1*R3/(Rd1+R3)=20Ohm*40Ohm/(20Ohm+40Ohm)=13.3Ohm
Rb1 and R1 connected in series so Ra1=Rb1+R1=13.3Ohm+40Ohm=53.3Ohm
The total resistance is Ra1 = 53.3Ohm
Now we calculate the current on R2
We know that the voltage between V1 nodes is 8 Volt.
All voltage generators except for V1 have been replaced with a short circuit.
All current generators have been replaced with an open circuit.
The components Rb1 and R1 connected in series.
The voltage between this components starting and ending node is 8 Volt
Rb1 is in the voltage divider so the voltage on Rb1 is Rb1/Ra1*8 Volt = 2 Volt
The current on Rb1 is the voltage on Rb1/Rb1 = 150m Amper
The components Rd1 and R3 connected in parallel. The voltage on Rd1 is 2 Volt because the voltage on Rb1 is 2 Volt
The current on Rd1 is the voltage on Rd1/Rd1 = 100m Amper
The components RGenZero0 and R2 connected in series.
The voltage between this components starting and ending node is 2 Volt
R2 is in the voltage divider so the voltage on R2 is R2/Rd1*2 Volt = 2 Volt
The current on R2 is the voltage on R2/R2 = 100m Amper
